observations.detail: RU-WB-M1 asked for bare «Окно»; the translator used «Контекстное окно». I OVERRULE the suggestion and accept the translator's deviation. Evidence: (a) the English sidecar for this key says 'The window is the context window', so the referent is the context window; (b) in the ru catalogue «окно» overwhelmingly means an app/dialog window or an analytics time window (56 values, e.g. «диалоговое окно», «в этом окне» = 'in this time window'), so a bare «Окно» here is ambiguous where the English 'The window' is not; (c) five shipped values already name this control «Контекстное окно» (ui.chat.pickers context_panel.context_window, context_panel.total_of_the_context_window, session_panel.context_window, session_panel.context_window_not_measured, session_panel.context_window_of). The translator's choice is the more consistent one.
observations.evidence: ru catalogue grep for 'онтекстн' and 'окн' (audit.log section A/tools); sidecar ui.chat.context.json

observations.detail: RU-WB-N3 (shorten the strip title) is RESOLVED and no meaning was lost: the English list is 'sign-in, settings and slash commands', and the new ru sentence names exactly those three («вход, настройки и slash-команды»). Dropping «в учётную запись провайдера» removes an addition the English never made. The ui.common.connection siblings still say «вход в учётную запись провайдера» because THEIR English says 'provider sign-in' - the divergence is correct, not an inconsistency.

RU-WB-N1 is RESOLVED. «Ваш вход по-прежнему сохранён.» replaces the physical metaphor «на месте» and matches the catalogue's own existing construction for the same fact: ui.settings.integrations.integration_model.the_sign_in_is_still_saved = «Вход всё ещё сохранён.», plus «Сохранённый вход» in ui.providers/ui.settings. The safety rule holds: it never implies the sign-in was lost or expired.
observations.evidence: ru catalogue grep for 'вход' (audit.log); sidecar note 'Never imply the sign-in was lost or expired'

observations.detail: The English value gained its closing backtick in this commit (3 -> 4). The ru value was already balanced (4) and is byte-identical across the commit; rendering it with the real formatter gives 4 literal backticks and a literal <token> (the ASCII apostrophes are ICU quoting and are consumed exactly as in English). Verified, not assumed.

Because every one of the nine ru catalogue files changed after its last audited bytes, NO carried-forward block is possible: ledger-rules binds each namespace block to the whole-file English AND target sha256, and all nine row pairs are stale at head (ledger-check: 25 ru findings before the rows are re-recorded, 1 of them 'ui.chat.status shipped without a ledger entry'). Hence a fresh nine-namespace receipt at full 62-key scope. CAVEAT for the coordinator: ledger-assemble preserves an existing row's historical `translator` identity (so ru/ui.chat keeps i18n-translator/deepseek-flash dated 2026-10-18 even though wave B amended its bytes); that is the tool's designed behaviour and matches what the other six locales will get. Updating translator provenance would be a deliberate hand edit, and should be done for all locales or none - I have not done it.

The prior audit's RU-WB-O4 stands unchanged: a user-supplied network name is inserted raw into «перемещается на {name}», which an adversarial name can bend. The value is byte-identical to the audited bytes, so it is not re-opened as a finding here; the locale-pattern note carries forward.
